scope: Correction learning and recall in installed Typeless, Doubao IME and Chatterfly: whether a user's edit of inserted dictation is detected, stored as vocabulary and used again. Ordinary-shell static observations of shipped bytes; no app launch, account, network request, user database or audio. EL-* IDs are local observations, not REA Evidence IDs. Offsets are byte offsets of a literal's first occurrence in the named file (Doubao's main executable is universal; each literal occurs once per slice).
method: Typeless literals were read through the inert rotated-literal decoding already used for competitor-rewrite.json (no target JavaScript executed). Doubao and Chatterfly were read with strings(1) and, for Chatterfly's four learned-term methods, objdump(1) call-site listings; no decompiler was available on this machine.

observations.finding: An edit tracker starts on IPC after insertion, requires an editable field whose full content contains the refined text, polls the focused field and keyboard, and settles on a 15 s timeout reset by each edit, a focus or input-box change, a cleared box, or Enter. A cleared box is judged by the last content read.

Over the first 1000 characters of the field: remaining length under 20 %, more than 50 % removed, or changes over twice the length is a large modification and is not reported; unchanged and cleared content is not reported either.

A small edit posts refined_inserted_text, original and edited input box, active application, device environment and mode, wrapped with context user_traits, to /user/traits. The response may carry auto_add_dictionary {term, user_dictionary_id}. The diff that yields the term is computed by the server.

The renderer shows a 5 s floating-bar alert naming the added term with an Undo button that deletes it by dictionary ID. The dictionary is an account resource behind /user/dictionary/{add,list,update,delete,batch-delete,bulk-import}.
No dictionary field was found in the /ai/voice_flow request construction; recall, if any, happens on the server per account. This is an inference from absence, not an observed server behaviour.

As the input method, Doubao snapshots the field after each ASR commit, records its own insert and delete-backward events, and settles before Return sends, on mouse settle candidates and when the next ASR round begins. A word diff that is too large is not uploaded.

Edits are uploaded to /api/v3/context/ime/modify_pair/v2; the sanitized modify pairs in the response are written into the local engine (GlobalContextAddModifyPair). User words go to /api/v3/context/ime/user_words.

A local SQLite table modify_pair keeps src/dst text (plaintext or encrypted columns with tags), use_count, recall_count and timestamps; entries expire after expire_days (default 30) and are evicted beyond a limit by update time and use count. A pair whose reverse also exists (A→B and B→A) is excluded from recall.

QueryModifyPairTopN takes today's pairs, then the highest recall_count, then the rest by use count up to total_limit, and fills the USER_MODIFY slot of the on-device speech-LLM prompt within user_modify_max_length. When a dst_text is recalled its recall_count increases.
SGVoiceEditTracker reads an accessibility baseline with anchors before and after the insertion, polls, settles on triggers and computes an edit distance. It reports only for a signed-in user (uid).

p_reportASRText:finalText:appContext:skillId: posts asr_text, final_text, app_context and uid as JSON to /speech/mining/term. The handler reads data.new_terms[].text and shows a learned-word view on the speech bar with an exposure beacon; the client does not store the term in this path.

YBVoiceDictSyncManager periodically calls the kernel's TriggerVoiceDictBuildSync, which fetches /lexicon/term/sync and builds a local VoiceUsrDict from VoiceTermRecord entries. Whether recognition or post-processing consumes that dictionary, or the server recalls by uid, was not established.
A separate punctuation learner settles the user's punctuation edits after speech per app.

limitations: Static reading only: defaults, consent gates, server-side diffing and the exact use of recalled terms were not observed at runtime.
Doubao offsets are in the universal file; the arm64 and x86_64 slices each contain the literal.
Chatterfly call sites come from objdump listings of four methods; the consumers of VoiceUsrDict were not traced.
